verdict.rationale: Kick documents role-based access control in which the owner decides who can see and do what. Its docs also describe an accountant adjusting the Chart of Accounts and reviewing, closing and locking periods, which shows accountant collaboration on the books. missing for 10: a documented invite flow for external users, named or defined roles (e.g. an accountant or bookkeeper role and its permissions), and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As a founder, I can invite my external accountant or bookkeeper with role-scoped access to review and adjust the books

citations.quote: Kick uses role-based access control so you decide exactly who can see and do what in your workspace.
you or your accountant can adjust it from there: adding, renaming, or restructuring accounts as needed
When your accountant finishes reviewing and closing a period, they lock it.
